sources.provider: Kappa Kappa Gamma, The Key magazine archive
sources.feature_id: Gamma Delta chapter history; separate cited 1952 issue: https://wiki.kkg.org/images/8/89/THE_KEY_VOL_69_NO_1_FEB_1952.pdf
sources.source_date: 1952-02 (The Key Vol. 69 No. 1, p.14); historical chapter page undated
sources.measurement_method: Historical text and black-and-white photograph; no scaled dimensions taken.
sources.observation: The 1952 caption identifies Gamma Delta’s present home, describes white rostone and the nickname “marble vault”; the article says it was built as a French Provincial chapter home of white rostone in 1935. The photo visibly shows two main facade levels, a steep mansard-like roof with dormers, regular windows with shutters, and a centered entry. Kappapedia chapter history says the site of the present chapter house was obtained in 1929 and the Waldron Street home became a reality in 1936–37.
sources.uncertainty: The photo is historical and no georeferenced camera view or measured elevation/plan is available. Source histories conflict slightly on construction year (1935 vs 1936–37). Current facade may have changed.
